text:
maria: FYI — Escalation from AcmeApps. They report repeated SSE disconnects when streaming completions. Partial output delivered, then client shows 'write EPIPE' and the stream stops. No 4xx in their server logs, connection simply drops after ~20-40s. Using our hosted EU cluster, model redwood/gpt-large-v1, SDK JS 0.10.1. Request id: req_9f3b7.

maria: Repro steps provided by customer: hit /v1/stream with Accept: text/event-stream, consume slowly (processing each event with a 200–400ms CPU-heavy callback). They say it used to work until last week.

customer-joe: there are no proxies on our side, just a node consumer that does heavy parsing per event. We see partial tokens in out.txt, then connection closed. Client log: `Error: write EPIPE` and `socket hang up`.

aj: can you paste the client/server logs and exact curl we should use to repro? also confirm any network appliances (cloudflare, nginx) in front.

maria: pasted their curl and minimal repro:

```
curl -N \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  "https://api.redwood.com/v1/stream?model=redwood/gpt-large-v1&request_id=req_9f3b7" > out.txt
```

customer-joe: here's a trimmed client trace: `2024-06-05T12:03:24.456Z ERROR write EPIPE at Socket._write (node:internal/streams/writable:...)`

dana: this smells like slow-consumer/backpressure on the TCP socket. If the client isn't draining the socket quickly, the kernel send buffer fills and subsequent writes fail. Our runtime has a defensive abort when write errors hit a threshold to avoid hung goroutines and memory leakage. We log it as `backpressure_threshold_exceeded`.

infra-oncall: grabbing the server-side stream trace now — found matching entries for req_9f3b7:

```
2024-06-05T12:03:18Z [stream] req=req_9f3b7 conn=10.2.3.45 write_buffer=0/65536
2024-06-05T12:03:21Z [stream] req=req_9f3b7 write: 32768/65536 (blocked)
2024-06-05T12:03:24Z [stream] req=req_9f3b7 write error: EPIPE
2024-06-05T12:03:24Z [stream] req=req_9f3b7 aborting stream: backpressure_threshold_exceeded
2024-06-05T12:03:24Z [runtime] req=req_9f3b7 held_tokens=132 partial_tokens_emitted=58
```

infra-oncall: note the write buffer filled and we hit our abort logic after ~3s of blocked write attempts. That corresponds to customer-reported timeline.

aj: thanks, that's useful. Two immediate customer-facing mitigations we can recommend: 1) switch to non-streaming completions (pull) while they fix client-side consumption speed, or 2) implement a streaming consumer that processes events asynchronously and drains the socket faster (e.g., push events to a work-queue and ack quickly). Also recommend retry logic with resume if they can tolerate duplicates.

maria: shared those workarounds with AcmeApps. They asked if we can increase buffer thresholds on hosted.

dana: we can tune thresholds but on hosted it affects multi-tenant resource management. Short-term I don't want to raise global thresholds. Longer term we can consider per-tenant soft limits or a configurable streaming throttle.

aj: can we provide an SDK-level helper to ease this? maybe our JS SDK could debounce heavy processing, or provide a built-in backpressure-aware reader that yields events and buffers a small queue.

dana: agreed — there's an open ticket in eng-runtime to add 'streaming backpressure docs + helper' (ENG-STREAM-576). We can prioritize if this class of customer hits >3 support tickets.

support-bot: Ticket #8792 created for AcmeApps (linked to req_9f3b7). Priority: P2.

maria: for triage, engineering asked for the following from the customer: full pcap/tcpdump for the session, Node version, exact SDK code that processes events, and whether any intermediate proxies (CF, ALB) exist. Also asked them to test with a minimal consumer that just writes events to /dev/null to confirm whether slow CPU is the root cause.

customer-joe: we'll try the /dev/null test and get the pcap. One quick note — they also tried with curl on a separate machine and saw the same disconnects, so it's likely client-side app behavior rather than one machine.

infra-oncall: added suggestion to run: `stdbuf -oL curl -N ...` and also `node --trace-sync-io` to rule out blocking JS sync IO during stream handling. If they can repro with a simple consumer that writes to /dev/null and still hit EPIPE, that's indicative of an intermediate network middlebox closing idle connections.

aj: action items:
- support: collect pcap + node trace + simple repro (maria)
- eng-runtime: review abort thresholds and logs for req_9f3b7 (dana/infra-oncall)
- devex: add a streaming consumer recipe to docs and a small JS helper in the SDK (assign to eng-devex)

maria: customer accepted workaround to temporarily use non-streaming mode; they will provide pcap tomorrow. I'll update the ticket when we have more. :thumbsup:

dana: long term note for product: consider a configurable per-tenant stream buffer or a 'graceful-suspend' behavior that signals the client (via SSE comment event) before aborting to improve debuggability.

maria: ok — closing loop for now. Will re-open if pcap shows different issue. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
